item.title: Bring Me Flesh: You Made Me Do It
item.content:encoded:
I've been reading SCPs for more than a decade and never bothered to join. Another story made me finally get an account to upvote it, but you are the first one to make me want to reply. This was a great, simple and well written creep-out. I love how you slip in the imagery with the little (Slurp, Slurp) and his crawling on the ceiling. Nothing explicit and yet the visuals for me were totally grotesque. Maybe I am just still in the Christmas mood.

+1 for sure.

item.title: SCP-5827:
item.content:encoded:
This seems like an excuse for a self insert and an excuse for using a drawing in one. There's not really going on with the anomaly or it's origin, holes that other comments mention even in almost non-existent scientific explanation. An intense focus on Nebula's personal life (which also pretty much doesn't exist) is in stark contrast to the cold and calculating nature of the foundation. Honestly I've seen better (imo) skips get discarded and I'd like to see this rewritten at the least.

As a personal aside I've been reading SCP for 6 years and I finally made an account because this broke the "suspension of belief" so hard for me and I wanted to voice that. Sorry, I don't want to discourage the writer and I believe this can be improved so it fits. This is all just my opinion

item.title: SCP-5243:
item.content:encoded:
I actually had a line about that in an older version of the skip! Originally there was a much more complicated calculation of how much containment damage the anomaly did — the first time's calculation was a September's worth of days times a set number, the next time's was an October's worth of days, so on and so forth — and whether or not it honoured leap years was actually going to matter, because there'd be one extra day when February rolled around and that would make a difference between near-total failure and total failure.

I didn't include any of that, because it was TOO FUCKING COMPLICATED lol

But yes, to answer the question you actually asked, the anomaly happens on September 8 no matter how many days there are in February. Because, luckily, it's magic and a teeny tiny bit sentient.

item.title: Canst thou draw out Leviathan with an Amortization? or his Tongue with a Bribe which thou lettest down?:
SCP-5104:
item.content:encoded:
Shouldn't the several hundred additional entities receive SCP designations? Shouldn't the Foundation perhaps take an interest in establishing communication with this species, if only in order to negotiate a less Veil-endangering place for them to portal in next time?

The Foundation presented in this scip seems amateurish and sloppy. Even compliant sentient entities are nontrivial to contain. It doesn't help that we're just offhandedly told that the second round of containment was successful, easy peasy, as if the evaluator is carefree and disinterested. There isn't even a cliché note about administering amnestics to witnesses.

I guess I'm in the minority, given that the article has 150+ upvotes. It's not all bad. I like the anomaly itself. I think its use of Yelp is cute, in a good way. But even the more cringe-inducing articles of the LOLFoundation era don't present this cavalier an institution.

item.title: Golan:
item.content:encoded:
I enjoyed this very, very much, although likely for reasons that other people didn't.

Namely, I'm very much into transformation fiction and you nailed so many of the little details that makes this kind of writing shine that I'm kind of in awe here.

It's that kind of extremely compelling body horror that is just… it's so good.
